requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
rationale:
The implementation and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.references.coverage.history`.

### Obligations and coverage

- **Include current on-disk contents, committed or not.** `src/coverage_history.rs#impl[RecentCoverage]/fn[load]` reads every existing evidence file before adding historical versions. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[uncommitted_records_count_as_they_are_on_disk]` verifies both that committed inputs survive an uncommitted reauthoring and that newly written inputs count immediately. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[deleting_the_only_record_that_read_an_item_warns_at_once]` verifies that deleting the existing record removes its window immediately.
- **Include the last N commits that changed each file.** `src/coverage_history.rs#impl[RecentCoverage]/fn[add_history]` tracks a separate version count per file, compares blobs against parent trees, and stops at the configured depth or the file's addition. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` checks retention and expiration at the default boundary, including independence from changes to another record. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_merge_counts_only_when_it_differs_from_every_parent]` checks the parent comparison; `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_shallow_clone_holding_every_window_is_complete]` also exercises an unrelated commit.
- **Read history through a Git library, not a `git` subprocess.** `src/coverage_history.rs#impl[RecentCoverage]/fn[add_history]` uses `git2` repository, revision-walk, tree, and blob APIs. Its reachable history helpers likewise use library APIs or file reads. The test fixtures' use of `git` constructs repositories rather than implementing history reads.
- **Ignore recorded hashes.** `src/coverage_history.rs#impl[RecentCoverage]/fn[add]` collects only file and selector from `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[outline_inputs]`; `src/coverage_history.rs#impl[RecentCoverage]/fn[covers]` compares selectors without hashes. `tests/references.rs#fn[items_named_by_recent_evidence_have_recent_coverage_whatever_their_hash]` verifies stale hashes and subsequent source edits, using ordinary evidence, citation reviews, and site reviews. Node containment is verified by `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[coverage_follows_the_outline_parent_chain_not_selector_text]`, including whole-file coverage and negative file/selector cases.
- **Take N from workspace `[coverage].reauthorings`.** `src/config.rs#fn[load_coverage_reauthorings]` and `src/config.rs#fn[coverage_reauthorings]` load the setting; `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]` applies it. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[the_window_follows_the_workspace_setting]` checks a one-version window.
- **Require a positive integer.** `src/config.rs#struct[CoverageConfig]` uses `Option<u32>`, and `src/config.rs#impl[CoverageConfig]/fn[validate]` rejects zero. The preceding window test checks zero rejection; `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_invalid_coverage_table_is_a_validation_finding_but_authoring_proceeds]` checks invalid types and diagnostics. Unknown-key diagnostics are specified by the same code's marked `requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`.
- **Default N to 3.** Both absent-file and absent-setting paths use `src/config.rs#const[DEFAULT_REAUTHORINGS]`, whose value is 3. The three-reauthoring test verifies the resulting default window.
- **Use available commits when history is unavailable.** `src/coverage_history.rs#impl[RecentCoverage]/fn[add_history]` retains successfully collected versions while reporting incomplete history. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[outside_git_only_the_files_on_disk_count_and_history_is_incomplete]`, `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_shallow_clone_uses_the_history_it_has_and_says_so]`, and `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_unreadable_historical_version_makes_history_incomplete]` assert the available coverage and incomplete flag. Referenced tests additionally cover linked worktrees and uncommitted records in shallow clones.
- **Have status and author report incomplete history.** `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_section]` renders the status notice; `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` renders the author notice. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts the status notice, and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics]` asserts the author notice outside Git. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about]` verifies that the notice remains present without item warnings.

### Integration and reachability

`src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_warnings]` reaches repository inspection and `src/commands.rs#fn[inspected_coverage_warnings]`, which invokes the history filter. `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]` supplies existing evidence and review files and the items left uncovered by current reference/evidence coverage. Its call to `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` applies the cited Rust-item coverage rules before historical coverage is considered. This preserves the cited requirement's role without reassessing its implementation here. The history collector, selector extraction, and containment checks are reachable from the subject's marked implementation roots.

No unacknowledged gap or obsolete acknowledgment was found.

{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.deleted_requirement
Function `render` is read only by the evidence of `requirements.cli.render`.
The requirement and its evidence file are deleted.
Deleted files have no coverage window, so `habeas status` warns about `render`
at once, before any further commit.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{example} coverage.uncommitted
The evidence of `requirements.cli.check` read `parse`. The requirement is
re-authored but not yet committed, and the new record does not read `parse`.
The committed versions in the window still name it, so `habeas status` does not
warn. If the new record had read `parse`, its contents on disk would cover it
even before the commit. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{example} coverage.shallow_clone
In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status` says that
coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents do not
cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{req} loading
An operation MUST load user configuration only when its requirements call for
user settings. A missing user file MUST represent absent user configuration;
whether the operation can proceed MUST be defined by the feature. Loading MUST
NOT create a file, repair malformed input, or supply an undocumented selection.
When loading configuration, Habeas MUST report unreadable files, invalid TOML,
unsupported user-file versions, unknown common keys, and invalid common field
types. It MUST validate the feature sections used by that operation and report
invalid feature settings with the file and setting identified. Unknown keys in
an explicitly documented provider-owned options map MUST follow that feature's
validation rules.
An operation MUST NOT require or semantically validate configuration for a
feature it does not use. This isolation MUST NOT suppress TOML syntax errors in
a shared file that the operation otherwise needs to parse. In particular,
ordinary validation still requires a parseable `book.toml` while remaining
independent of authoring settings and the user configuration file. It MUST apply
the selected workspace's evidence path policy without loading its model clients
or credentials.
:::{req} workspace_structure
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`habeas.toml` MUST serialize WorkspaceConfig as UTF-8 TOML with `version = 1`.
Its supported feature tables are `[authoring]`, `[coverage]`, and
`[evidence]`; each MAY be absent. `[coverage]` has one optional key,
`reauthorings`, under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`; it has
no user-file counterpart or invocation option, and no operation requires it. Unknown keys, unsupported versions, and invalid field types MUST produce
a diagnostic identifying the file and setting. Invalid TOML, including content
that is not UTF-8, MUST produce a diagnostic identifying the file, with the line
and column of a syntax error.
Features MUST define their own data structures and loading rules under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`. A file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid. Habeas settings MUST NOT require a `[habeas]` table
inside `book.toml`.
